source.section: PDF page 18, Schedule S Part B Line 18 (interest on obligations of the United States, such as treasury notes and bills); PDF page 14, Lines 11, 14, 15

worked: Federal AGI = wages 40,000.00 + U.S. Treasury interest 4,000.00 + bank interest 750.00 = 44,750.00. Projection: the Line 18 deduction is not_modelled (warn_when never), so the Treasury interest is taxed. Federal taxable income = 44,750.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 29,000.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). D-400 Line 6 federal AGI 44,750.00. Line 7 additions (Schedule S Part A) 0.00. Line 8 = Line 6 + Line 7 = 44,750.00. Line 9 deductions (Schedule S Part B) 0.00. Line 10 child deduction 0.00 (no qualifying children). Line 11 NC standard deduction (single) 12,750.00. Line 12a = Lines 9 + 10 + 11 = 12,750.00; Line 12b = Line 8 - Line 12a = 32,000.00. Line 14 NC taxable income (full-year resident) = 32,000.00. Line 15 tax = 32,000.00 x 0.0425 = 1,360.00. Line 16 credits 0.00; Line 17 income tax = 1,360.00. The booklet itself would deduct 4,000.00 on Schedule S Line 18: Line 12b = 44,750.00 - 4,000.00 - 12,750.00 = 28,000.00, tax 1,190.00; the projection overstates tax by 170.00 (4.25% x 4,000.00).
accepted_approximations: Interest on U.S. Treasury obligations is taxed (the projection cannot tell it from other interest).
